::: {.why}
Five months ago you wrote a specification for this trade and deferred it; today it goes through the same pipeline as every other signal, which is the test of whether the pipeline was general enough.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Evaluate a variance risk premium signal through the standard pipeline and report it against the noise floor.
- Say what its return distribution looks like and why the Sharpe ratio understates the risk.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Build and evaluate it: a time-series signal that is short variance when the implied-realized gap is wide and flat otherwise, sized by your standard rules, with a cost assumption that reflects option spreads rather than equity spreads. Run it through qlib/signals/report.py and generate the page.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Report what the standard metrics miss: the skew and kurtosis of monthly returns, the worst month, and the drawdown distribution from a simulation. Then state plainly that a Sharpe ratio computed on a payoff this asymmetric is not comparable to one from your equity signals, and say what you would report instead.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
The variance risk premium signal joins the book, evaluated through the same pipeline as everything else, with an explicit note that its Sharpe ratio is not comparable to the equity signals' because of the payoff asymmetry.
:::
